researched_by: KCC's own Let's Talk Kent traffic order consultations and permanent traffic order guidance, the KCC order notices and statements of reasons published by Folkestone & Hythe District Council as KCC's TRO agent, KCC country park parking pages, Dover District Council's caravans and motorhomes guidance, and contemporaneous local news reporting
policy_summary:
SCOPE NOTE: Kent County Council is the local highway and traffic authority for the whole of Kent except Medway, which is unitary. It makes every on-street traffic regulation order in the twelve districts, and every on-street parking place in Kent is designated by a KCC order. IT DOES NOT OWN THE CAR PARKS. Off-street parking in Kent belongs to the districts - Thanet, Dover, Folkestone & Hythe, Canterbury, Swale, Ashford, Maidstone, Tonbridge & Malling, Tunbridge Wells, Sevenoaks, Dartford and Gravesham - and each publishes its own off-street parking places order. Thanet District Council states the split plainly: on-street TROs are Kent County Council's, off-street TROs are the district's. Every motorhome bay, every overnight car park tariff and every 'no sleeping' condition in Kent is a DISTRICT instrument and is researched separately. Nothing in this file is about a district car park.

There is NO county-wide Kent prohibition on overnight parking, on sleeping in a vehicle, or on motorhomes in lay-bys, and KCC publishes no county-level motorhome policy at all. Its parking pages cover yellow lines, blue badges, residents' schemes and nuisance parking, and the nuisance parking page pushes motorhome and caravan complaints straight to the districts or the police. What KCC has instead is a coastal town-by-town pattern: named lengths of seafront road added to district consolidation orders as motor-caravan prohibitions, always overnight, always after residents complained.

Three such regimes were found, all on the Channel and North Sea coast, all administered by the district on KCC's behalf. THANET: an overnight ban on motor caravans parking 6pm-6am on Cliff Road and The Parade (Birchington), Sea Road (Westgate), Royal Esplanade (Westbrook) and Palm Bay Avenue (Margate). Proposed in July 2021 after complaints about mess, noise and sightlines at Palm Bay Primary School; the consultation has closed and the order has been made. RAMSGATE: from 1 September 2020 overnight parking on Western Undercliff and Royal Harbour Approach is restricted to cars and motorcycles between 6pm and 6am - a class restriction that catches a campervan as surely as a coachbuilt motorhome. FOLKESTONE & HYTHE: Amendment 8 to the KCC (Various Roads, Folkestone and Hythe) (Waiting Restrictions and Street Parking Places) (Consolidation) Order 2025 proposed a motorhome parking ban 6pm-7am on Sandgate Esplanade, Sandgate High Street, Granville Parade, Granville Parade West, Metropole Road East and West, Cliff Road, Marine Parade, Marine Parade Mews, Marine Crescent, Lower Sandgate Road West, Military Road in Hythe and Dymchurch Road between Scanlons Bridge and Red Lion Square. Representations closed 5pm on 5 December 2025; no 'has made' notice was found.

Against that, KCC's street parking places carry ONE genuine piece of provision. On Marine Parade and Waterloo Crescent on Dover seafront, motorhomes and caravans are barred 8am-6pm but may park overnight for GBP13 paid at the machine - a paid on-street stopover ten minutes from the ferry terminal, and the only place in Kent where the highway itself is offered to a motorhome for the night. Dover District Council administers and collects it.

The port dimension matters but is mostly not about motor caravans. KCC operates a Kent-wide overnight lorry parking prohibition enforced by clamping - a GBP150 release fee plus a GBP35 penalty - across Ashford, Canterbury, Dover, Folkestone & Hythe, Maidstone, Swale and Thanet, with designated lay-bys on the A249, A299 and A256 and commercial truck stops as the sanctioned alternatives. Operation Brock and Dover TAP queue freight on the M20 and A20 when the Short Straits back up. None of this is aimed at leisure vehicles, but it is why Kent's A-road lay-bys are signed, watched and often full of lorries.
notes:
The instrument shape is the thing to record. Kent has not written a county-wide motor caravan schedule the way Devon did. It amends each district's consolidation order separately, so the same policy appears three times under three different order titles, advertised by three different district transportation departments, and there is no single Kent document that lists where motorhomes are banned. TraffWeb, KCC's mapping application, has no motor caravan legend layer either - the restriction is carried as an ordinary waiting prohibition with a vehicle-class qualification, so it is invisible unless you read the order schedule. A van user cannot find this out from any KCC page.

The division of labour is unusually clean and unusually confusing. The district councils draft, advertise and consult on KCC's orders, take representations to a Joint Transportation Board, and then enforce them under civil parking enforcement - but the order is KCC's. That is why the Folkestone & Hythe motorhome ban is published on folkestone-hythe.gov.uk under a Kent County Council order title, and why residents consistently blame the wrong council.

Direction of travel: tightening, and accelerating. Ramsgate 2020, Thanet 2021, Folkestone & Hythe 2025, with a further Amendment 17 out to consultation until April 2026 converting seasonal restrictions on The Parade and Coast Drive at Greatstone and Lydd on Sea to all-year. The 2025 Sandgate proposal is the widest yet - thirteen named roads across three towns in one amendment - and it is the first Kent order to be advertised in terms as a 'motorhome parking ban' rather than buried in a schedule.

Enforcement reality is mixed. On-street the sanction is a penalty charge notice, which for a resident-nuisance problem is weak; a PCN does not move a vehicle. Where KCC has actually had to clear people out it has used land powers, not parking powers. In June 2026 it served 24-hour notices to leave on 19 caravans, campers and motorhomes on its own land at Ramsgate's Western Undercliff after welfare checks, some of which had been there for over a year. That is the tell: the 6pm-6am sign had been up since 2020 and had not shifted long-term occupation.

KENT'S OTHER LAND. KCC runs nine country parks - Shorne Woods, Trosley, Manor Park, Lullingstone, Teston Bridge, Brockhill, Grove Ferry, Pegwell Bay and Hothfield. They are not aires and cannot become them: car parks are locked at dusk and Shorne Woods, checked as representative, has a 2m height barrier. No overnight or motorhome policy is published for any of them.

NO LAY-BY MOTOR-CARAVAN ORDER WAS FOUND. The A2, A20, A256, A249 and A299 lay-bys carry freight controls, not leisure-vehicle ones. Kent has not used TROs against motorhomes on its trunk and primary route lay-bys.

The Canterbury district consolidation order was read in full as a control: it contains no motor caravan, motorhome, caravan or overnight provision anywhere. So the three coastal regimes really are exceptions, not a pattern spread across the county.
open_questions: The made date and order title for the Thanet overnight motor caravan ban. The Let's Talk Kent page says the consultation has concluded and the order has been made, but the sealed order and its schedule of lengths could not be retrieved - the document links on letstalk.kent.gov.uk return 404.

Whether Amendment 8 to the KCC (Various Roads, Folkestone and Hythe) (Waiting Restrictions and Street Parking Places) (Consolidation) Order 2025 has been made. Representations closed 5 December 2025 and no 'has made' notice was published on the district site by July 2026. It is recorded here as draft.

The formal vehicle-class wording in the Folkestone & Hythe order. The proposal notice and Sandgate Parish Council both call it a 'motorhome parking ban'; Kent orders elsewhere use 'motor caravan'. Whether the restriction bites on DVLA body type or on something broader is unresolved, and it decides whether a converted panel van is caught.
Exact lengths of road for all three restrictions. None of the retrievable notices gave metre-by-metre schedules, so the map records are street-level at best.

Whether the Ramsgate restriction is drafted as 'cars and motorcycles only' (a permissive parking place) or as a prohibition on other classes. It changes who gets a PCN - the former catches a Transit as well as a motorhome.

Who sets the GBP13 overnight motorhome tariff on Dover's Marine Parade and Waterloo Crescent, and under which order. Dover District Council publishes the rule; the parking places themselves are on the highway and should therefore sit in a KCC order. Dover's own seafront notice (Order No. 59, 2018) covers only coach bays and does not mention motorhomes.

Whether KCC's overnight lorry parking clamping regime reaches leisure vehicles. Reporting describes it as applying to 'vehicles of over five tons', which would in principle catch a large A-class; the underlying order was not obtained and it is almost certainly drafted against goods vehicles.
Whether KCC has ever considered a county-wide overnight or coastal-corridor motor caravan restriction. No committee paper proposing one was found.

What legal basis KCC used to clear Western Undercliff in June 2026 - land-owner powers, Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 s.77/78 direction, or something else. The reporting says 'notice to leave' without citing the power.

sites.name: Cliff Road and The Parade (Birchington), Sea Road (Westgate), Royal Esplanade (Westbrook) and Palm Bay Avenue (Margate)
sites.notes: The Thanet coastal limb of KCC's regime: no motor caravans parking any day between 6pm and 6am on five named seafront roads spread across three towns, so no single coordinate is honest. Proposed in July 2021 after Birchington, Westgate and Margate residents complained about mess, noise, lost residents' spaces and large vehicles blocking sightlines by Palm Bay Primary School; KCC's stated reasons are the statutory ones - avoiding danger to persons or other traffic and facilitating the passage of traffic including pedestrians. The Let's Talk Kent page records that the consultation has closed and the order has been made, but the sealed order was not retrievable, hence medium confidence. NOTE THE INTERLOCK: Royal Esplanade is the road Thanet District Council's Barnes car park sits on, and Barnes has five paid overnight motorhome bays. KCC pushes motor caravans off the kerb; the district takes them in fifty metres away. Neither council's page tells you the other half.

sites.name: Western Undercliff and Royal Harbour Approach, Ramsgate
sites.notes: In force since 1 September 2020. Overnight parking between 6pm and 6am is restricted to CARS AND MOTORCYCLES ONLY, which is why this is recorded as applying to all vehicles rather than to motor caravans specifically - it catches a campervan, a converted panel van and a coachbuilt motorhome equally, whether or not anyone is asleep in it, and it does not depend on a DVLA body type. Cllr Kup's October 2025 motion to the district council cites this as the 2020 Traffic Regulation Order that displaced motorhomes onto Ramsgate's residential streets. The sign has not been enough on its own: in June 2026 KCC served 24-hour notices to leave on 19 caravans, campers and motorhomes occupying its land here, after welfare checks, some having been in place well over a year.
sites.geocode_precision: pin on Royal Harbour Approach at the head of Ramsgate's Royal Harbour; the same restriction extends west along Western Undercliff, roughly a kilometre away, which this pin does not cover

sites.name: Sandgate, Folkestone and Hythe seafront roads (proposed motorhome ban 6pm-7am)
sites.notes: Amendment 8 to the Kent County Council (Various Roads, Folkestone and Hythe) (Waiting Restrictions and Street Parking Places) (Consolidation) Order 2025 - the widest single motorhome measure yet advertised in Kent, covering thirteen named roads: Sandgate Esplanade, Sandgate High Street, Granville Parade, Granville Parade West, Metropole Road East, Metropole Road West, Cliff Road, Marine Parade, Marine Parade Mews, Marine Crescent, Lower Sandgate Road West, Military Road in Hythe, and Dymchurch Road in Hythe between Scanlons Bridge and Red Lion Square. Advertised on 10 November 2025 with representations due by 5pm on Friday 5 December 2025, addressed to Folkestone & Hythe District Council's Transportation department acting for KCC. Statement of reasons gives only the standard formula - securing the expeditious, convenient and safe movement of traffic and preventing danger or obstruction. NO 'HAS MADE' NOTICE WAS FOUND by July 2026, so this is recorded as draft; it may well be in force. Note the 7am end, an hour later than the Thanet and Ramsgate orders.

sites.name: Marine Parade and Waterloo Crescent, Dover (on-street overnight motorhome parking)
payment_methods: pay and display machine on site
sites.notes: THE ONLY PLACE IN KENT WHERE THE HIGHWAY ITSELF IS SOLD TO A MOTORHOME FOR THE NIGHT, and the mirror image of every other record in this file. Motorhomes and caravans may NOT park on Marine Parade or Waterloo Crescent between 8am and 6pm, but overnight parking is permitted for GBP13 paid at the on-street machines. Ten minutes' walk from the Port of Dover, which is why it is the best-known stopover on the Kent coast and why van forums have tracked it for years - it was free overnight until the charge came in. No facilities, no waste point, and it is a seafront main road: users consistently report traffic noise all night and vehicles passing close. Recorded in the KENT COUNTY COUNCIL file because it is on-street and therefore a KCC parking place, but DOVER DISTRICT COUNCIL publishes the rule, sets the tariff and enforces it - do not duplicate this record if Dover District Council is researched separately. Which order actually designates it is unresolved; Dover's own published seafront notice covers coach bays only.
sites.geocode_precision: pin on the Marine Parade seafront kerb at Dover, from the Campercontact stopover listing; Waterloo Crescent continues immediately west along the same frontage

sites.name: All Kent County Council country parks
sites.notes: KCC's nine country parks - Shorne Woods, Trosley, Manor Park, Lullingstone, Teston Bridge, Brockhill, Grove Ferry, Pegwell Bay and Hothfield - are the council's only significant off-street estate, and none of them is available overnight. The car parks are locked daily at dusk, and Shorne Woods, checked as representative, publishes a 2m height barrier that excludes almost every motorhome and most high-top campervans outright. Horseboxes, coaches and minibuses have a published GBP9 day tariff; motor caravans have no tariff at all. There is no published overnight, camping or motorhome policy for any of the nine, and the physical arrangements make one unnecessary. Included so the map does not suggest that KCC's own land is an option.
